podcast.title: Collaboration with Steve Albini
podcast.body: The legendary producer Steve Albini, known for his work with Nirvana and Pixies, also worked on albums with The Breeders. "This is from a 2009 album entitled Him to the Immortal Wind, which is a big fan favorite and recorded by the legendary Steve Elbeni, who did all those albums with Nirvana and the Pixies and the Breeders and Bush."

podcast.title: Early Funding and Hiatus
podcast.body: Kim Deal secured $11,000 from The Pixies' UK record label to record a demo, which eventually became their album "Pod." Following its release, the band went on hiatus as Kim returned to The Pixies and Tanya Donnelly rejoined Throwing Muses. "She sent a demo to the Pixies record label in the UK and they gave her $11,000 to record a demo."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation as an Outlet
podcast.body: The Breeders were formed by Kim Deal, the bassist for The Pixies, because she was frustrated that her original songs were not being recorded by her primary band, and she sought an outlet for her own material. "Kim was really frustrated because she had written a bunch of songs that she knew would never be recorded by the Pixies, so this band became her outlet."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation from Pixies Frustration
podcast.body: The Breeders were formed by Kim Deal, who was frustrated by her inability to contribute more creatively to the Pixies. The band was described as an "almost all-female band." "When Kim became frustrated with not being able to contribute more to the Pixies, she formed an almost all-female band called The Breeders with Kelly Unlead Guitar."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Indie Alternative Act
podcast.body: Fronted by sisters Kim and Kelley Deal, The Breeders were a significant indie alternative act in the early part of the decade. "The breeders, fronted by Kim and Kelly Deel, who were a big indie alternative act early in the decade."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

podcast.title: Kelly Deal's Legal Troubles
podcast.body: Kelly Deal, Kim's sister and band member, faced legal issues when she was caught accepting a FedEx package containing heroin, which took several years to resolve. "But then Kelly got busted when she accepted a FedEx package full of heroin and that took a couple of years to sort out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 2

podcast.title: Kim Deal's Side Project
podcast.body: The Breeders originated as Kim Deal's side project while she was still a member of The Pixies. After The Pixies' breakup, she developed it into a full-time band with her sister, Kelly Deal. "Kim Deel remade the breeders, her Pixies side project, into a full-time thing with her sister Kelly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 2

podcast.title: Knitting Hobby and Online Store
podcast.body: Kelly Deal is proficient at knitting and operates an online store where she sells unique, handmade scarves. These scarves, which are either knitted or crafted from recycled felt and wool sweaters, are one-of-a-kind, signed by her, and typically retail for around $100 each. "all are one of a kind hand made by her and signed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Reactivation After Pixies Breakup
podcast.body: The Breeders were reactivated after The Pixies broke up, leaving Kim Deal free to focus on new songs and return to the studio with her band. "But then the Pixies broke up and Kim was without anything to do, so the breeders were reactivated, some new songs were written, and the band returned to the studio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Return After Hiatus
podcast.body: The band had not released an album for approximately 10 to 12 years prior to this new release. Many younger listeners might not be familiar with them due to this long break. "Hace como 10 o 12 años que sacó su último disco."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Similar Sound to Pixis
podcast.body: The band's sound is noted for being very similar to that of the Pixis, stemming from Kindle La Chica's involvement with both groups. "son muy parecidos a los Pixis."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Touring with Nirvana
podcast.body: A year after Kelly Deal started playing guitar, The Breeders embarked on a tour with Nirvana, highlighting their rapid rise in the music scene. "A year later, the breeders were off touring with Nirvana."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Career Transition to Professional Knitting
xref.body: After a career that included success with The Breeders and other bands, Kelly Deal transitioned to become a professional knitter, specializing in handbags, and has even released a book of patterns. "These days, she's a professional knitter, especially as handbags. She's even released a book of patterns."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Collaboration with Steve Albini
xref.body: The legendary producer Steve Albini, known for his work with Nirvana and Pixies, also worked on albums with Godspeed You! Black Emperor. "This is from a 2009 album entitled Him to the Immortal Wind, which is a big fan favorite and recorded by the legendary Steve Elbeni, who did all those albums with Nirvana and the Pixies and the Breeders and Bush. And here we go again, Godspeed you, Black Emperor."

xref.title: Defense Contractor Career
xref.body: Before joining The Breeders, Kelly held a job with a defense contractor, which included having a top-secret clearance. "By the time the breeders came along, Kelly had a job with a defense contractor complete with a top secret clearance."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Engineer for Iconic Albums
xref.body: Albini engineered several highly acclaimed albums, including Pixies' "Surfer Rosa" (1988), The Breeders' "Pod" (1990), PJ Harvey's "Rid of Me," and most notably, Nirvana's "In Utero," playing a crucial role in its sound. "Steve Elbeany was a very big part of the sound of Inuro."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Identical Twin and Untrained Guitarist
xref.body: Kelly Deal is the identical twin sister of Kim Deal, the original bassist for the Pixies. In 1992, Kelly joined Kim in The Breeders as the guitarist, despite having no prior experience playing the instrument, quickly learning and mastering it. "She was the guitarist. And to be honest, she knew nothing about the instrument. She did not know how to play, but she was a fast learner and nailed it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Late Start on Guitar
xref.body: She started playing the guitar for the first time at the age of 30, convinced by her sister Kim to join The Breeders. "So she started playing the guitar for the first time at age 30."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Breakup Careers and Challenges
xref.body: Following the breakup, members pursued diverse paths: Black Francis became Frank Black, releasing solo albums; Kim Deal transformed her side project, The Breeders, into a full-time band with her sister Kelly (who later faced legal issues after being busted for heroin); drummer David Lovering became "the scientific phenomenalist," a magician, but struggled financially; and guitarist Joey Santiago found success as a composer for TV and film, contributing to shows like "Weeds." "Everybody scattered. Black frances renamed himself Frank Black and released a string of solo albums, Kim Deel remade the breeders, her Pixies side project, into a full-time thing with her sister Kelly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
